title: Best Free CRM for Small Businesses (2026)
dek: A free CRM can run a small business well — until you hit a wall you did not see coming. This guide covers what "free" really means, which free CRMs are genuinely useful, and the exact limits (users, contacts, automation) that tell you it is time to pay.

seo.metaTitle: Best Free CRM for Small Businesses (2026)
seo.metaDescription: The best free CRMs for small business, and what "free" really means — the user, contact and automation limits that tell you when it is time to pay.

richText: A free CRM is a real category, not a trick — several established vendors offer a plan that never expires. The catch is that "free" is defined by limits, and knowing where those limits sit is the difference between a free CRM that carries you for a year and one you outgrow in a month. This guide explains what free actually includes, which options are worth starting with, and the signs it is time to upgrade.

body.richText: A free forever plan is not a free trial — it does not end after 14 days. Instead, vendors cap it in ways designed to be comfortable for a very small team and to nudge you upward as you grow. The caps that matter most are:

items: Free tiers commonly allow only a handful of people on the account.
There is often a ceiling on how many contacts or deals you can store.
Multi-step workflows and sequences are usually reserved for paid plans.
Two-way email sync and some connectors may be paid-only.
Free tools can carry vendor branding and offer limited support.

body.text: HubSpot Free — the most generous starting point

body.richText: HubSpot's free CRM stands out for pairing contact and deal management with light marketing, forms, and email in one free account. It is the easiest way to look professional from day one. The trade-offs are a small user cap, a single pipeline, HubSpot branding on free assets, and automation that is largely paid-only.

body.text: Zoho CRM Free and Freshsales Free — real CRM features at zero cost

body.richText: Zoho CRM's free edition gives a small team genuine CRM functionality — leads, contacts, deals, and basic reports — and Freshsales' free tier adds built-in email to a simple sales workflow. Both are solid homes for a couple of people running a sales process without paying yet.

richText: small sales teams who want structure, not just a contact list.

body.text: Capsule and Bigin — simple and free for the smallest teams

richText: If you want the least complexity, Capsule's free tier suits very small, contact-first tracking, and Bigin (Zoho's lightweight CRM) gives a solo owner or micro-team a clean pipeline for free. These are ideal starting points that you can grow out of gently. For a deeper look at options aimed at one-person businesses, see

link.text: the best CRM for freelancers and solo owners

body.richText: Three signals usually mean it is time to pay: you have added people and hit the user cap; you are storing so many contacts that the record limit is close; or you keep wanting automation — reminders, sequences, workflows — that only paid plans unlock. If none of those bite yet, staying free is the right call.

items.question: Is there a genuinely free CRM, or is it always a trial?
items.answerRichText: Several vendors — including HubSpot, Zoho, Freshsales, and Capsule — offer a free forever plan, not just a trial. It is limited by users, contacts, and features, but it does not expire, so a small team can run on it indefinitely if it fits within the caps.

items.question: What is the best free CRM for a very small team?
items.answerRichText: HubSpot's free CRM is the most generous all-rounder, while Zoho and Freshsales free tiers suit small sales teams and Capsule or Bigin suit the simplest setups. The best pick depends on how many users you need and whether you also want marketing or just a pipeline.

items.question: When should I upgrade from a free CRM?
items.answerRichText: Upgrade when you outgrow the user cap, approach the contact or record limit, or repeatedly need automation that only paid plans include. Until one of those limits actually slows you down, a free plan is usually enough.
